clue.text: Top hat is wrong with trews

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters of hat is and trews are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict: wearing a top hat with tartan trousers is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top hat' reads as one item of headwear, but 'Top' alone is the definition. TREWS are close-fitting tartan trousers, traditionally Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshirt is a loose casual garment worn on the upper body, which clothing shops call a top.

clue.text: Longed for the audience perspective

indicators.note: what the audience hears is the spoken sound, so the word for longed for is taken by ear

parts.note: to have sighed for something is to have longed for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearned for the view from the seats in the stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longed for' gives SIGHED, which sounds the same as the answer when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in an argument is one particular viewpoint or angle on it, as in 'see his side of things'.

clue.text: Old flyer for show

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-husband
PO is Pilot Officer, an RAF rank, so a flyer

explanation.surface: An old aircraft or pilot is on display at an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a short form of exposition, a large public exhibition or show of goods.

clue.text: Bishop and cardinal following God ought almost to be full-blooded

indicators.note: following puts the bishop and cardinal letters after the god and the shortened word

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

indicators.note: almost means the word ought loses its final letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
cardinal red is the vivid scarlet of a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: A churchman's remark that clergy following God ought to be wholehearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman beside the bishop, but here it is the colour of a cardinal's robes. 'almost' removes the final T of 'ought', giving OUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred horse is of pure pedigree, so full-blooded in breeding terms.

clue.text: Items of headgear have truncated flap

indicators.note: truncated means each piece of headgear is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a hood is one item worn on the head
a hat is a second item worn on the head

explanation.surface: Hats with clipped brims are flapping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Items' is plural, so two pieces of headwear are wanted: HOOD and HAT; 'truncated' cuts off D and T to give HOO and HA.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a state of fuss or commotion, and a hoo-ha is a noisy fuss over something trivial.

clue.text: Old soldier with bullet going to the front

parts.note: a round is a single bullet or shell
the head of a queue or column is its front

explanation.surface: A veteran rushes to the front line carrying ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUNDHEADS were the Parliamentarian soldiers of the English Civil War (1642-51), named for their short-cropped hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roundhead was a soldier of the Parliamentary army in the seventeenth-century English Civil War, hence an old soldier.

clue.text: Stone circle: luxurious place to sit back

parts.note: O is circular in shape

indicators.note: sit back hints that the seat word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: one sits in the lap of luxury

explanation.surface: A stone circle seems a comfortable place to lean back and rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone circle' looks like Stonehenge, but 'Stone' alone is the definition. The 'lap of luxury' gives LAP; 'back' turns it to PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The opal is a precious gemstone known for its shifting play of colours.

clue.text: Spy blowing whistle perhaps on test that's coming up

parts.note: a peep is a short high whistle, so peeping is sounding one

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the test letters read upwards

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK vehicles, run by the old Ministry of Transport

explanation.surface: A whistleblower spills secrets about an upcoming exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT test, read upwards in the down light, gives TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeping Tom is a voyeur who secretly watches others, so a kind of spy.

clue.text: What late risers do, say —- and late rulers?

definitions.note: the definition stands for what dead monarchs do before burial, a verb phrase to fit the clue's opening

parts.note: people who rise late lie in bed
to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: Slugabeds and dead kings both stay lying down, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' shifts sense: risers who get up late, rulers who are dead. 'What ... do' governs both halves, so the definition reads as 'what late rulers do'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceased monarchs are displayed publicly in a coffin before burial, which is the custom called lying in state.

clue.text: "Dinosaur" disrespectful term for CID man, old copper's concluding

indicators.note: concluding puts the copper's letters at the very end of the word

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, an officer of the CID, Britain's plain-clothes police branch
Plod is a mocking British name for the police, after Mr Plod in the Noddy books
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A detective is mockingly called a dinosaur by an old-fashioned constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, the same sense as Plod, but it is the metal, symbol CU, with its 's giving S.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplodocus was a huge long-necked plant-eating dinosaur of the late Jurassic period.

clue.text: Odd characters leaving after the party

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions depart, keeping only the even ones from the two words after the

explanation.surface: Strange people walk out once the celebration has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' looks like eccentric guests; it means letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of AFTERTHE go, leaving FETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festival or celebratory gathering, often held to raise funds.

clue.text: Prince and king ensconced beneath elaborate grand balcony comfortably

indicators.note: settled beneath, so in this down entry the royal letters sit below the reworked ones
elaborate means intricately worked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is a standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A prince and king settle down below an ornate grand balcony at their ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' rearranges G and BALCONY into BYALONGC; HAL and K go beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: By a long chalk is a British idiom meaning by a wide margin, so winning comfortably.

clue.text: Cat going after bottle tossed in rowdy local

definitions.note: in British slang bottle is courage, which this big cat seeks

indicators.note: letters tossed about are jumbled, so in and rowdy local are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub brawler puts a bottle through the window of the rowdy local.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wizard of Oz lion goes to the wizard in search of courage, which is 'bottle' in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cowardly Lion is the timid big cat in The Wizard of Oz who journeys to gain courage.

clue.text: Dresses, including hat, lifted and carried high!

indicators.note: lifted in a down entry means the whole is read from the bottom upwards
including means the hat letters are placed within the dressing word

parts.note: to enrobe someone is to dress them in a robe
a cap is a type of hat

explanation.surface: Dresses and a hat are hoisted aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures clothes hoisted aloft; 'lifted' in a down light means the whole assembly reads upwards, so ENROBECAPS is entered from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaceborne describes something carried through space, high above the earth.

clue.text: Tad wrong, pocketing righteous folk's small change!

indicators.note: pocketing means the scrambled letters take the rest inside them, as in a pocket
wrong means the word tad is put out of its order

parts.note: the just are righteous people, so just men

explanation.surface: A slightly crooked person helps themselves to good people's loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' looks like loose coins; it is a minor alteration. 'wrong' rearranges the letters of Tad as ADT, split around the righteous men.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustment is a minor alteration, so a small change in an arrangement.

clue.text: Class exercises, eager, captivated by outstanding teacher

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise taken as a school class

indicators.note: captivated means held captive inside, so eager sits within the outstanding word

parts.note: a debt outstanding is due
agog means eagerly expectant

explanation.surface: Keen exercises in class are held by an excellent teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise; it means unpaid, DUE, which holds AGOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster or instructor, often a strict or pedantic one.

clue.text: Time for Matt, perhaps, to put nice disguise on?

definitions.meaning: when the glossy paint is finished, it is time for the matt finish, read as a phrase about paint
to hide flaws by giving a pleasing appearance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Matt' looks like a man's name; it is the dull paint finish, the opposite of gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss over a fault is to conceal it beneath a smooth, attractive surface treatment.

clue.text: Split showing above board

definitions.meaning: British slang for run away quickly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' and 'leg it' are both slang for leaving in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is slang for legitimate, meaning lawful and honest, and leg it means flee.

clue.text: Very little comfort perhaps and not quite enough goodness!

indicators.note: not quite enough means the exclamation stops one letter short of the end

parts.note: crumbs is a mild British exclamation like goodness

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how little consolation there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' looks like virtue; it is the exclamation 'Goodness!', which 'Crumbs!' also is.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount of consolation is called a crumb of comfort, a crumb being a scrap.

clue.text: Thoroughly cleaned after excessive amount of drug that's left over

indicators.note: after places the cleaning words behind the drug abbreviation

parts.note: OD is an overdose
a room done out has been thoroughly cleaned

explanation.surface: After an overdose, someone's place is scrubbed clean and what remains is cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd one out is the single item remaining when others are paired or grouped.

clue.text: Sweet comes out with cold fluff round the edges

indicators.note: the bungle word goes round the edges of the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to fluff a task is to botch it
to come out with words is to utter them
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A dessert emerges with frozen fluffy decoration around its rim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out' looks like the definition of a verb, but 'comes out with' together give UTTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard sweet made from butter and brown sugar.

clue.text: Wise young sergeant major upped and cancelled service

indicators.note: upped in a down clue means the rank letters are read upwards

parts.note: a sergeant major is a Warrant Officer, WO
in tennis a let is a serve that must be retaken

explanation.surface: A youthful sergeant major was promoted and his religious service called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise young' is a cryptic definition: owls are proverbially wise, and their young are owlets.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls stand for wisdom in folklore, so their chicks, owlets, are young of the wise bird.

clue.text: Maid immodestly holding up skirt

indicators.note: up in a down clue means those letters read upwards
holding means the words maid immodestly contain the letters

explanation.surface: A maid shamelessly hitches up her skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' finds AIDIM in 'mAID IMmodestly'; 'up' reads it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a skirt whose hem falls to mid-calf.

clue.text: Ancient royal head: first century

indicators.note: first puts the century letter before the head word

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A royal head of a former age, dating from the first century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a ruler; it is NUT. CNUT, or Canute, was an eleventh-century king of England, Denmark and Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Cnut was an eleventh-century Danish king who ruled England, so an ancient royal.

clue.text: Wind blows making one do this?

definitions.meaning: to wind in a fishing line on a spool
being punched makes a person stagger

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests gales; 'Wind' is the verb, as with a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is both to wind a line onto a spool and to stagger dizzily after being struck.

clue.text: Reckoning line's replaced chapter in Exodus

indicators.note: replaced means the line letter takes the place of the chapter letter

parts.note: an exodus is a mass departure or evacuation
L is an abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Bible study: a verse in Exodus is swapped for a different chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exodus' looks like the book of the Bible; it is a mass departure.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation is an assessment or appraisal, a reckoning of value.

clue.text: Heads for seaside, taking an early return fare

indicators.note: return means the initials are read in reverse order
heads are the first letters of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Seaside trippers catch an early return train with packed food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads for seaside' reads like a journey; it takes S, T, A, E, which 'return' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, which is also called fare.

clue.text: Time to try kiss, turning red

indicators.note: turning means the words to try kiss are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone blushes when the moment comes to attempt a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like a blush; it is a communist, here a follower of Leon Trotsky.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trotskyist follows Trotsky's revolutionary communism, and red is slang for a communist.
